title: SLO fanout hardening: heterogeneous circuit breaker mismatch and multi-region cache warmup spike
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Summary: On 2026-02-18 we observed a sustained SLO breach for 20m affecting text-generation latency p95 across several customers in eu-west-1 and us-west-2. Root behavior: a global cache warmup combined with regionally inconsistent circuit breaker thresholds and an autoscaler overshoot produced a cross-region amplification of requests. This ticket captures the incident synthesis, immediate mitigations, and the hardening plan to prevent recurrence.
timeline: 2026-02-18T09:12:00Z - Alert: p95 latency > SLO (hosted-api: text-gen) for eu-west-1. Pager triggered.
2026-02-18T09:15:00Z - Engineering on-call triaged: high error budget consumption, elevated tail latencies; metrics show spike in GPU scheduling latency and queue depth.
2026-02-18T09:18:00Z - Temporary mitigation: increased circuit-breaker leniency in eu-west-1 via feature flag to avoid immediate client failures while we investigated.
2026-02-18T09:25:00Z - Observed peering traffic: several failover rules routed requests from eu-west-1 to us-west-2; us-west-2 began experiencing degraded p95 within 6 minutes.
2026-02-18T09:32:00Z - Autoscaler in eu-west-1 launched additional pods to handle queue; warmup caused KV cache misses and heavy KV population IO, driving sustained GPU scheduling delays.
2026-02-18T09:40:00Z - Mitigation: applied emergency rate-limiter at the edge (token-bucket) to cap cross-region fanout and prevented further amplification.
2026-02-18T09:50:00Z - Metrics stabilized after rate limit and rollback of aggressive autoscale policy; SLO returned under threshold by 09:58.
2026-02-18T10:05:00Z - Incident declared resolved. Post-incident work captured in this ticket.
root_cause: Three compounding factors: (1) KV cache flush/invalidations during autoscaler-driven replacement caused a high volume of cold-core KV population work, increasing per-request latency; (2) circuit breaker thresholds were tuned differently across regions (eu-west-1 allowed higher concurrent in-flight requests than us-west-2), enabling upstream failovers to amplify load into regions with tighter limits; (3) autoscaler policy used aggressive scale-up without staged warmup which caused simultaneous cold starts across many replicas.
mitigations: Applied emergency global rate-limit for cross-region failover traffic to cap fanout
Rolled back recent autoscaler policy change that removed staggered ramp-ups
Temporarily relaxed CB tripping in the most impacted region to reduce client errors while we stabilized
action_items: ENG-17346: Standardize circuit breaker semantics across regions (owner: Liam O'Connor, estimate: 3) - ensure same failure thresholds and cooldown behavior for region-local and cross-region requests

ENG-17347: Implement staged replica warmup and KV prefetch hooks in the autoscaler (owner: Mei Tan, estimate: 8) - prepopulate hot KV prefixes and stagger pod readiness to avoid synchronized cache misses
ENG-17348: Add cross-region fanout caps at the request-router layer with per-tenant burst tokens (owner: Carlos Ruiz, estimate: 5) - configurable per-customer and tied to SLA tier
ENG-17349: Create automated SLO-alert playbook that correlates CB tripping, autoscale events, and KV miss rate to trigger proactive mitigation (owner: Priya Sharma, estimate: 3)
ENG-17350: Run chaos experiment (simulated cold-cache and burst failover) in staging to verify protections (owner: Reliability Team, estimate: 5)
